newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts expected carryover technical demand in live cattle following the surge to 10-month highs Friday on active speculative fund buying. Expectations that cash cattle could trade $1 per cwt higher at $70 this week could also lend support, they said.
However, others considered the market overbought and look for cash markets to decline and pressure futures.

Boxed beef values have been working lower as retailers finished purchases for Memorial Day and packers will need fairly large slaughter supplies only for another week. Cash prices will go down next week if they manage to hold this week. The seasonal trend is down into June, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to show carryover demand following the higher CME feeder cattle index and expected setback in grain futures. Corn futures are seen declining on the expected large corn crop, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.28 to $73.36 per cwt, highest level since February 16, 1995.
